Row numbers, grouped headers, density

<poad-table>

Three reading aids: a “#” column that numbers the rows following the page, a header row that gathers columns under a shared title, and a button that tightens the rows.

import { Component, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { PoadColumnComponent, PoadTableComponent } from '@poadio/ui-angular';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-table-grid-demo',
  imports: [PoadTableComponent, PoadColumnComponent],
  template: `
    <!-- toutes les colonnes ont une largeur : une colonne de remplissage prend le reste -->
    <poad-table [value]="services" dataKey="id" title="Services" showRowNumber [headerGroups]="groups" showDensityToggle [(dense)]="dense"
      resizableColumns paginator [rows]="5">
      <poad-column field="name" header="Service" width="110px" />
      <poad-column field="env" header="Env" width="80px" />
      <poad-column field="owner" header="Owner" width="120px" />
      <poad-column field="pods" header="Pods" dataType="number" width="70px" />
    </poad-table>
    <code>dense={{ dense() }}</code>
  `,
})
export default class TableGridDemo {
  readonly groups = [{ header: 'Service', span: 2 }, { header: 'Team', span: 2 }];
  readonly services = [
    ['web-01', 'prod', 'Front office', 4], ['api', 'neo', 'Fleet team', 2], ['worker', 'neo', 'Night jobs', 1], ['web-02', 'prod', 'Front office', 3],
    ['gateway', 'prod', 'Fleet team', 2], ['billing', 'recette', 'Back office', 1], ['search', 'neo', 'Front office', 3], ['mailer', 'recette', 'Night jobs', 1],
    ['auth', 'prod', 'Fleet team', 2], ['reports', 'neo', 'Back office', 1], ['cache', 'prod', 'Fleet team', 2], ['cron', 'recette', 'Night jobs', 1],
  ].map(([name, env, owner, pods], i) => ({ id: i + 1, name, env, owner, pods }));
  readonly dense = signal(false);
}

Next.js uses the same package as React: the demo is rendered by @poadio/ui-react. The code shows the App Router integration — a client component ('use client') for state, rendered by a server page.

// app/table-grid-demo.tsx — client component (state, handlers)
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { PoadTable, type PoadTableColumn } from '@poadio/ui-react';

interface Service { id: number; name: string; env: string; owner: string; pods: number }
const SERVICES: Service[] = ([
  ['web-01', 'prod', 'Front office', 4], ['api', 'neo', 'Fleet team', 2], ['worker', 'neo', 'Night jobs', 1], ['web-02', 'prod', 'Front office', 3],
  ['gateway', 'prod', 'Fleet team', 2], ['billing', 'recette', 'Back office', 1], ['search', 'neo', 'Front office', 3], ['mailer', 'recette', 'Night jobs', 1],
  ['auth', 'prod', 'Fleet team', 2], ['reports', 'neo', 'Back office', 1], ['cache', 'prod', 'Fleet team', 2], ['cron', 'recette', 'Night jobs', 1],
] as const).map(([name, env, owner, pods], i) => ({ id: i + 1, name, env, owner, pods }));
// toutes les colonnes ont une largeur : une colonne de remplissage prend le reste
const columns: PoadTableColumn<Service>[] = [
  { field: 'name', header: 'Service', width: '110px' },
  { field: 'env', header: 'Env', width: '80px' },
  { field: 'owner', header: 'Owner', width: '120px' },
  { field: 'pods', header: 'Pods', dataType: 'number', width: '70px' },
];
const groups = [{ header: 'Service', span: 2 }, { header: 'Team', span: 2 }];

export default function TableGridDemo() {
  const [dense, setDense] = useState(false);
  return (
    <>
      <PoadTable value={SERVICES} columns={columns} dataKey="id" title="Services" showRowNumber headerGroups={groups} showDensityToggle
        dense={dense} onDenseChange={setDense} resizableColumns paginator rows={5} />
      <code>dense={String(dense)}</code>
    </>
  );
}

// app/page.tsx — server component: HTML rendered on the server, hydrated on the client
import TableGridDemo from './table-grid-demo';

export default function Page() {
  return <TableGridDemo />;
}

What it is for

For lists people quote or compare (“row 12”), wide tables whose columns come in families, and screens where more rows should fit at once. showRowNumber adds the “#” column before the selection; numbers follow the page (page 2 of 5 rows starts at 6), server-side data included, and restart from the displayed rows in groups or trees. headerGroups takes a list of { header, span, class? }: each title covers span displayed columns, in order; technical columns (numbers, selection, actions) keep an empty cell. showDensityToggle puts the “Density” button at the end of the toolbar; density is dense, controlled or not: dense / defaultDense / onDenseChange in React, v-model:dense in Vue, [(dense)] in Angular, the web component’s dense property and densechange event. Finally, when every column of a resizableColumns table has a width, an empty filler column takes the remaining room: each column keeps exactly its width and the handle follows the pointer to the pixel (see “Column width”). In cards, neither grouped headers nor filler.

Keyboard

KeyEffect
TabReaches the toolbar’s “Density” button (numbers and grouped headers are not tab stops).
Enter SpaceOn “Density”: tightens or loosens the rows.

Accessibility

  • The “Density” button is a toggle button: aria-pressed="true" when rows are tight; the root then carries is-dense.
  • Each grouped header is a <th scope="colgroup" colspan>: a screen reader announces it with the columns it covers. Its row counts in aria-rowcount and in the aria-rowindex of the rows below.
  • The filler column is empty and hidden from assistive technologies (aria-hidden); it adds no cell to read and no tab stop.
Stylesheets, theme tokens and texts stylesheets to import, 34 tokens, catalogue texts

Stylesheets to import

Nothing to import for this component: it bundles its own sheet (@poadio/ui-core/table.css, @poadio/ui-core/paginator.css, @poadio/ui-core/icon.css) at build time. Only tokens.css and base.css are loaded once, globally (see Installation).

How to change

In the application’s global stylesheet, after the @poadio/ui-core sheets: on :root for the whole application, or on a container for one area only. A floating layer (menu, list, dialog) may be rendered outside its container: for it, prefer :root.

src/styles.css
/* The whole application */
:root {
  --poad-accent: #0b7a5c;        /* Accent colour: primary button, checked box, selection */
  --poad-radius: 4px;            /* Corner rounding of controls */
}

/* In dark theme only */
.theme-dark {
  --poad-accent: #3fcf9f;        /* Accent colour: primary button, checked box, selection */
}

/* One area only */
.checkout {
  --poad-radius: 0;              /* Corner rounding of controls */
}

Open the demo full screen

What it is for

For tables users arrange themselves (dashboards, long lists). columnMenu puts the ⋮ button on every header; a column opts out with menu: false. The menu is the library’s (keyboard, “Pin” submenu, focus back on the button); its items follow the column: sorting only if it is sortable, “Hide column” as long as another one stays visible (hideable: false forbids it), “Filter…” (a filterable column) moves focus into its cell of the filter row, “Choose columns…” (with columnToggle) opens the toolbar’s chooser with focus on the first checkbox, “Reset columns” restores widths, pinning, hidden columns, order and sorting (the resetColumns() method does the same, reset() resets the whole table). columnMenuItems replaces the default items, columnMenuExtra adds your items at the bottom of the menu (after a separator); columnMenuAction reports each choice. The table keeps the state; to keep it from one visit to the next, control it: pinnedColumns / hiddenColumns (onColumnPin, onHiddenColumnsChange in React, v-model:pinned-columns / v-model:hidden-columns in Vue, web component properties). With the group zone, the menu also offers “Group by”. In Angular, columnMenu defaults to auto (a menu as soon as a column is sortable or filterable).

Keyboard

KeyEffect
TabReaches the ⋮ button of each column that has a menu.
Enter SpaceOpens the menu, focus on its first item.
↓ ↑ Home EndMoves through the menu items.
→Opens the “Pin” submenu (← closes it).
EscCloses the menu; focus returns to the ⋮ button (also after a choice, except “Filter…” and “Choose columns…”, which move it into the filter or the chooser).

Accessibility

  • The ⋮ button is a real <button> named “Column menu, Pods”, with aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded; the menu is the library’s role="menu", its items are menuitems.
  • The button stays visible when the column is sorted or filtered, on focus and on a touch screen (no hover).

What it is for

For tables users arrange themselves (dashboards, long lists). reorderableColumns puts the handle on every movable header; a column keeps its place with reorderable: false, and frozen columns (pinned, sticky) do not move, nor do technical columns (selection, actions). The table keeps the order; to keep it from one visit to the next, control it with columnOrder (column ids: onColumnReorder in React, v-model:column-order in Vue, [(columnOrder)] in Angular, the web component’s columnOrder property) — a column added later keeps its declared place. The column menu’s “Reset columns” restores the declared order. The side panel (Columns tab) reorders too, with the same handle, top to bottom. In cards (small screens), no handle.

Keyboard

KeyEffect
TabReaches the handle of each movable header.
Space EnterGrabs the column, then drops it; focus stays on its handle.
← →Moves the grabbed column (reversed right to left).
Home EndFirst or last place.
EscCancels: the column goes back to its place.

Accessibility

  • The handle is a real <button> named “Move column Pods”, described by a hint giving the keys.
  • Each step is said in an aria-live region: “Column Pods grabbed, position 2 of 3”, its new place, the drop or the cancel.
  • With a finger, the handle has touch-action: none: the gesture does not scroll the page.

How to change

In the application’s global stylesheet, after the @poadio/ui-core sheets: on :root for the whole application, or on a container for one area only. A floating layer (menu, list, dialog) may be rendered outside its container: for it, prefer :root.

src/styles.css
/* The whole application */
:root {
  --poad-accent: #0b7a5c;        /* Accent colour: primary button, checked box, selection */
  --poad-radius: 4px;            /* Corner rounding of controls */
}

/* In dark theme only */
.theme-dark {
  --poad-accent: #3fcf9f;        /* Accent colour: primary button, checked box, selection */
}

/* One area only */
.checkout {
  --poad-radius: 0;              /* Corner rounding of controls */
}

import { Component, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { PoadColumnComponent, PoadTableComponent, type PoadColumnToggleEvent } from '@poadio/ui-angular';

@Component({
  selector: 'app-table-column-chooser-demo',
  imports: [PoadTableComponent, PoadColumnComponent],
  template: `
    <poad-table [value]="services" dataKey="id" title="Services" columnToggle reorderableColumns [columnMenu]="true" (columnToggled)="toggled($event)">
      <poad-column field="name" header="Service" [toggleable]="false" />
      <poad-column field="env" header="Env" filterable />
      <poad-column field="owner" header="Owner" />
      <poad-column field="pods" header="Pods" dataType="number" />
    </poad-table>
    <code>hidden={{ hidden().join(',') }}</code>
  `,
})
export default class TableColumnChooserDemo {
  readonly services = [
    { id: 1, name: 'web-01', env: 'prod', owner: 'Front office', pods: 4 },
    { id: 2, name: 'api', env: 'neo', owner: 'Fleet team', pods: 2 },
    { id: 3, name: 'worker', env: 'neo', owner: 'Night jobs', pods: 1 },
    { id: 4, name: 'web-02', env: 'prod', owner: 'Front office', pods: 3 },
  ];
  /** Colonnes masquées (ids) : la case du sélecteur et « Masquer la colonne » émettent `columnToggled`. */
  readonly hidden = signal<string[]>([]);
  toggled(e: PoadColumnToggleEvent): void {
    const id = e.column.id();
    this.hidden.update((h) => (e.hidden ? [...h.filter((x) => x !== id), id] : h.filter((x) => x !== id)));
  }
}

What it is for

For a wide table where everyone keeps the columns they need. columnToggle puts the “Columns” button in the toolbar (label: columnsLabel); the panel lists every column, hidden ones included, in display order. A hideable: false column (Angular: [toggleable]="false") has its checkbox greyed out, and the last shown column cannot be hidden. With reorderableColumns, each line has “Move up” and “Move down”: the same order, and the same event, as dragging the headers. With columnMenu, each column’s menu gains “Choose columns…”, which opens this panel, and, for a filterable column, “Filter…”, which moves focus into its cell of the filter row. Hidden columns are the same state as the column menu’s “Hide column”: control it to keep it (hiddenColumns / onHiddenColumnsChange in React, v-model:hidden-columns in Vue, the web component’s hiddenColumns property, (columnToggled) in Angular). In cards, no button.

Properties

NameTypeDefaultDescription
booleanfalse“Columns” button to hide, show (and reorder) columns.

booleanfalseReordering by dragging headers (CDK); order can be persisted through [(columnOrder)] (ids = key|field|header).
boolean | 'auto''auto'⋮ menu per header (default: auto = if sorting, filtering, reordering, column chooser or grouping is possible).
T[]—Rows of the table (without data).

Below, the <PoadTable> properties specific to this feature; all the others are described in Data table.

NameTypeDefaultDescription
boolean—Column chooser in the toolbar (“Columns” button): one checkbox per column to hide or show it (hiddenColumns) and, with reorderableColumns, Move up / Move down buttons (columnOrder). Escape closes it; the column menu’s “Choose columns…” opens it. Not in cards.
string—Label of the column chooser button; default: the catalogue’s table.columns message.
boolean—A handle at the start of every header to change the column order by dragging (mouse, finger) or with the keyboard (Space, ← →, Space; Escape cancels). Frozen columns, reorderable: false and technical columns (selection, actions…) keep their place. Not in cards.
boolean—⋮ button on every header (except menu: false): the library's menu with sorting, pinning at the start or the end, width fitting, “Hide column”; columnMenuExtra adds the application's items.
readonly T[]—Rows of the table (without data).

Keyboard

KeyEffect
Enter SpaceOn the “Columns” button: opens or closes the panel. On a checkbox: shows or hides the column.
Tab Shift+TabMoves through the checkboxes and the Move up / Move down buttons; leaving the panel closes it.
EscCloses the panel; focus returns to the “Columns” button.
↓ ↑ Home EndIn the column menu (Enter on ⋮): down to “Choose columns…” (focus on the first checkbox) or “Filter…” (focus in the column’s filter), then Enter.

Accessibility

  • The button follows the “disclosure” pattern: a real <button> named “Columns”, aria-expanded, aria-controls pointing to the panel. The panel is a role="group" named like the button, not a menu: it holds checkboxes, not menu items.
  • Each checkbox is the library’s, named after its column header; a column that cannot be hidden has its checkbox disabled. The “Move up” / “Move down” buttons are disabled at the top and bottom of the list.
  • Focus is never lost: Escape gives it back to the button, “Choose columns…” puts it on the first enabled checkbox, “Filter…” on the first control of the filter cell.

How to change

In the application’s global stylesheet, after the @poadio/ui-core sheets: on :root for the whole application, or on a container for one area only. A floating layer (menu, list, dialog) may be rendered outside its container: for it, prefer :root.

src/styles.css
/* The whole application */
:root {
  --poad-accent: #0b7a5c;        /* Accent colour: primary button, checked box, selection */
  --poad-radius: 4px;            /* Corner rounding of controls */
}

/* In dark theme only */
.theme-dark {
  --poad-accent: #3fcf9f;        /* Accent colour: primary button, checked box, selection */
}

/* One area only */
.checkout {
  --poad-radius: 0;              /* Corner rounding of controls */
}

Table filters

<poad-table>

A global search in the toolbar and a filter row under the header: one field per filterable column, an operator menu (contains, starts with, between, empty…), values to tick, a typing delay, and an “N rows · filtered · selected” footer.

Filters sit on <poad-column> (filterable, filterType, [filterOptions]); the state is [(filters)] and [(globalFilter)], (filterChange) reports gestures.

import { Component, signal } from '@angular/core';
import { PoadColumnComponent, PoadTableComponent, type PoadFilterChangeEvent } from '@poadio/ui-angular';

interface Project { id: number; name: string; env: string; pods: number }

@Component({
  selector: 'app-table-filters-demo',
  imports: [PoadTableComponent, PoadColumnComponent],
  template: `
    <div class="demo-wide">
      <poad-table [value]="projects" dataKey="id" title="Projects" showSearch showRowCount (filterChange)="changed($event)">
        <poad-column field="name" header="Name" sortable filterable />
        <poad-column field="env" header="Env" filterable filterType="select" [filterOptions]="envs" />
        <poad-column field="pods" header="Pods" dataType="number" sortable filterable />
      </poad-table>
    </div>
    <code>filters={{ active() }}</code>
  `,
})
export default class TableFiltersDemo {
  readonly projects: Project[] = [
    { id: 1, name: 'gestion', env: 'recette', pods: 4 }, { id: 2, name: 'inventaire', env: 'neo', pods: 0 },
    { id: 3, name: 'demo2', env: 'neo', pods: 2 }, { id: 4, name: 'best', env: 'recette', pods: 12 },
    { id: 5, name: 'démo10', env: 'recette', pods: 1 }, { id: 6, name: 'atlas', env: 'neo', pods: 7 },
  ];
  readonly envs = [{ label: 'recette', value: 'recette' }, { label: 'neo', value: 'neo' }];
  readonly active = signal('none');
  changed(e: PoadFilterChangeEvent): void {
    this.active.set([...Object.keys(e.filters).filter((k) => e.filters[k]), ...(e.globalFilter ? ['search'] : [])].join(',') || 'none');
  }
}

Next.js uses the same package as React: the demo is rendered by @poadio/ui-react. The code shows the App Router integration — a client component ('use client') for state, rendered by a server page.

// app/table-filters-demo.tsx — client component (state, handlers)
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { PoadTable, type PoadTableColumn, type PoadTableFilterEvent } from '@poadio/ui-react';

interface Project { id: number; name: string; env: string; pods: number }
const projects: Project[] = [
  { id: 1, name: 'gestion', env: 'recette', pods: 4 }, { id: 2, name: 'inventaire', env: 'neo', pods: 0 },
  { id: 3, name: 'demo2', env: 'neo', pods: 2 }, { id: 4, name: 'best', env: 'recette', pods: 12 },
  { id: 5, name: 'démo10', env: 'recette', pods: 1 }, { id: 6, name: 'atlas', env: 'neo', pods: 7 },
];
const envs = [{ label: 'recette', value: 'recette' }, { label: 'neo', value: 'neo' }];
const columns: PoadTableColumn<Project>[] = [
  { field: 'name', header: 'Name', sortable: true, filterable: true },
  { field: 'env', header: 'Env', filterable: true, filterType: 'select', filterOptions: envs },
  { field: 'pods', header: 'Pods', dataType: 'number', sortable: true, filterable: true },
];

export default function TableFiltersDemo() {
  const [active, setActive] = useState('none');
  const changed = (e: PoadTableFilterEvent) =>
    setActive([...Object.keys(e.filters).filter((k) => e.filters[k]), ...(e.globalFilter ? ['search'] : [])].join(',') || 'none');
  return (
    <>
      <div className="demo-wide">
        <PoadTable value={projects} columns={columns} dataKey="id" title="Projects" showSearch showRowCount onFilterChange={changed} />
      </div>
      <code>filters={active}</code>
    </>
  );
}

// app/page.tsx — server component: HTML rendered on the server, hydrated on the client
import TableFiltersDemo from './table-filters-demo';

export default function Page() {
  return <TableFiltersDemo />;
}

filters and globalFilter are held by the element: a gesture emits filterchange (detail { filters, globalFilter }), a value set by the page is rendered without an event. Custom filter: renderFilter.

<script type="module">import '@poadio/ui-elements/define';</script>

<div class="demo-wide">
  <poad-table id="filtered" data-key="id" heading="Projects" show-search show-row-count
    columns='[{"field":"name","header":"Name","sortable":true,"filterable":true},
              {"field":"env","header":"Env","filterable":true,"filterType":"select","filterOptions":[{"label":"recette","value":"recette"},{"label":"neo","value":"neo"}]},
              {"field":"pods","header":"Pods","dataType":"number","sortable":true,"filterable":true}]'></poad-table>
</div>
<code id="filters-out">filters=none</code>

<script type="module">
  const table = document.querySelector('#filtered');
  table.value = [
    { id: 1, name: 'gestion', env: 'recette', pods: 4 }, { id: 2, name: 'inventaire', env: 'neo', pods: 0 },
    { id: 3, name: 'demo2', env: 'neo', pods: 2 }, { id: 4, name: 'best', env: 'recette', pods: 12 },
    { id: 5, name: 'démo10', env: 'recette', pods: 1 }, { id: 6, name: 'atlas', env: 'neo', pods: 7 },
  ];
  table.addEventListener('filterchange', (e) => {
    const { filters, globalFilter } = e.detail;
    const active = [...Object.keys(filters).filter((k) => filters[k]), ...(globalFilter ? ['search'] : [])];
    document.querySelector('#filters-out').textContent = `filters=${active.join(',') || 'none'}`;
  });
</script>

What it is for

To find rows in a fully loaded table: matching ignores accents and case in the page’s language, numbers and dates are read as typed. Filters are inputs of the table and its columns (filterable, filterType, filterOptions); their state { [field]: { value, matchMode } } can be held by the application. With server-side data (lazy), the table emits the state without filtering: the server answers. The side panel and the filter chip have their own pages.

PoadTableColumn

Below, the PoadTableColumn properties specific to this feature; all the others are described in Data table.

NameTypeDefaultDescription
boolean—Filterable column: a field in the filter row.
'text' | 'number' | 'date' | 'boolean' | 'select'—Filter type (text, number, date, boolean, select): chooses the operators and the input field.
readonly TableFilterOption[]—Choices of the select filter: { label, value }[].

Keyboard

KeyEffect
TabMoves from a filter field to its operator button, then to its clear button.
Enter SpaceOn the operator or values button: opens its menu; in the menu: picks (the values menu stays open).
↓ ↑In a menu: next / previous item.
EscCloses the menu and gives focus back to its button.

Accessibility

  • Each field is named after its column (“Filter Name”, bounds “(min)” / “(max)”); the operator button says the current operator (“Operator: Contains”).
  • The filter row counts in aria-rowcount and shifts the rows’ aria-rowindex; menus are named role="menu" (“Filter operator”, “Filter values”).
  • Yes / no and single choice go through the library’s dropdown, never a native <select>.

Next.js uses the same package as React: the demo is rendered by @poadio/ui-react. The code shows the App Router integration — a client component ('use client') for state, rendered by a server page.

// app/filter-chip-demo.tsx — client component (state, handlers)
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { PoadFilterChip } from '@poadio/ui-react';

export default function FilterChipDemo() {
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<string | null>(null);
  return (
    <>
      <div className="demo-row">
        <PoadFilterChip label="Status" value={status ?? ''} active={!!status} onClick={() => setStatus('online')} onRemove={() => setStatus(null)} />
        <PoadFilterChip label="Owner" icon="plus" removable={false} />
      </div>
      <code>status={status ?? 'none'}</code>
    </>
  );
}

// app/page.tsx — server component: HTML rendered on the server, hydrated on the client
import FilterChipDemo from './filter-chip-demo';

export default function Page() {
  return <FilterChipDemo />;
}

<script type="module">import '@poadio/ui-elements/define';</script>

<div class="demo-row">
  <poad-filter-chip id="status-chip" label="Status"></poad-filter-chip>
  <poad-filter-chip label="Owner" icon="plus" removable="false"></poad-filter-chip>

<code id="chip-out">status=none</code>

<script type="module">
  const chip = document.querySelector('#status-chip');
  const show = (status) => {
    Object.assign(chip, { value: status ?? '', active: !!status });
    document.querySelector('#chip-out').textContent = `status=${status ?? 'none'}`;
  };
  chip.addEventListener('press', () => show('online'));
  chip.addEventListener('remove', () => show(null));
</script>

What it is for

To show, above a table, the few filters people set often. The chip filters nothing itself: the application opens its editor on click and removes the filter on ×. The value text is computed with tableFilterChipValue (values, bounds, dates in the language).

    { id: 3, name: 'demo2', env: 'neo', pods: 2, owner: 'Noël' }, { id: 4, name: 'best', env: 'recette', pods: 12, owner: 'Hélène' },
    { id: 5, name: 'atlas', env: 'neo', pods: 7, owner: 'Zoé' },
  ];
  readonly envs = [{ label: 'recette', value: 'recette' }, { label: 'neo', value: 'neo' }];
  readonly active = signal('none');
  changed(filters: PoadFilters): void {
    this.active.set(Object.keys(filters).filter((k) => filters[k]).join(',') || 'none');
  }
}

Next.js uses the same package as React: the demo is rendered by @poadio/ui-react. The code shows the App Router integration — a client component ('use client') for state, rendered by a server page.

// app/table-panel-demo.tsx — client component (state, handlers)
'use client';

import { useState } from 'react';
import { PoadTable, PoadTablePanel, type PoadTableColumn, type TableFilters } from '@poadio/ui-react';

interface Project { id: number; name: string; env: string; pods: number; owner: string }
const projects: Project[] = [
  { id: 1, name: 'gestion', env: 'recette', pods: 4, owner: 'Hélène' }, { id: 2, name: 'inventaire', env: 'neo', pods: 0, owner: 'Zoé' },
  { id: 3, name: 'demo2', env: 'neo', pods: 2, owner: 'Noël' }, { id: 4, name: 'best', env: 'recette', pods: 12, owner: 'Hélène' },
  { id: 5, name: 'atlas', env: 'neo', pods: 7, owner: 'Zoé' },
];
const envs = [{ label: 'recette', value: 'recette' }, { label: 'neo', value: 'neo' }];
const COLUMNS: PoadTableColumn<Project>[] = [
  { field: 'name', header: 'Name', sortable: true, filterable: true },
  { field: 'env', header: 'Env', filterable: true, filterType: 'select', filterOptions: envs },
  { field: 'pods', header: 'Pods', dataType: 'number', sortable: true, filterable: true },
  { field: 'owner', header: 'Owner' },
];

export default function TablePanelDemo() {
  const [columns, setColumns] = useState(COLUMNS);
  const [filters, setFilters] = useState<TableFilters>({});
  const [search, setSearch] = useState('');
  return (
    <>
      <div className="demo-wide" style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'stretch' }}>
        <PoadTable value={projects} columns={columns} dataKey="id" title="Projects" showFilterRow={false} filters={filters} globalFilter={search}
          onFilterChange={(e) => { setFilters(e.filters); setSearch(e.globalFilter); }} style={{ flex: 1, minWidth: 0 }} />
        <PoadTablePanel columns={columns} onColumnsChange={setColumns} filters={filters} onFiltersChange={setFilters} globalFilter={search} onGlobalFilterChange={setSearch} />
      </div>
      <code>filters={Object.keys(filters).filter((k) => filters[k]).join(',') || 'none'}</code>
    </>
  );
}

// app/page.tsx — server component: HTML rendered on the server, hydrated on the client
import TablePanelDemo from './table-panel-demo';

export default function Page() {
  return <TablePanelDemo />;
}

<poad-table-panel for="table-id"> (or the table property): as in Angular, the panel sets columns, filters and globalFilter on its table and redraws on each of its renders. poad-* tags being display: contents, the table’s width is given to a wrapper (<div style="flex: 1">).

What it is for

For a wide table whose columns are chosen and which is filtered without the filter row. The panel acts on the table (same columns, same filters): what changes on one side shows on the other. Below 768 px it overlays the table, closed by default. The Groups and Values (aggregates) tabs are described with row groups.

Keyboard

KeyEffect
↓ ↑On a rail tab: next / previous tab (wrapping).
Home EndFirst / last tab.
Enter SpaceOpens the tab, or closes the panel on the open tab; on a filter header: expands or collapses it.

Accessibility

  • Rail as the WAI-ARIA “tabs” pattern: vertical role="tablist", a single tab stop (the active tab), aria-selected, aria-controls to the role="tabpanel" named by its tab.
  • Each column has its checkbox named by its label, the “all” checkbox goes to the mixed state; each filter header is an aria-expanded button.

Nothing to import for this component: it bundles its own sheet (@poadio/ui-core/table-panel.css, @poadio/ui-core/table.css, @poadio/ui-core/checkbox.css, @poadio/ui-core/select.css, @poadio/ui-core/option-list.css, @poadio/ui-core/floating.css, @poadio/ui-core/number.css, @poadio/ui-core/datepicker.css, @poadio/ui-core/segmented.css, @poadio/ui-core/icon.css) at build time. Medium shadow: raised element0 4px 6px rgba(0,0,0,.07)0 4px 6px rgba(0,0,0,.4)
Strong shadow: menus, dialogs, notifications0 12px 24px rgba(15,23,42,.08)0 12px 24px rgba(0,0,0,.5)
Stacking order of floating layers100002same

How to change

In the application’s global stylesheet, after the @poadio/ui-core sheets: on :root for the whole application, or on a container for one area only. A floating layer (menu, list, dialog) may be rendered outside its container: for it, prefer :root.

src/styles.css
/* The whole application */
:root {
  --poad-accent: #0b7a5c;        /* Accent colour: primary button, checked box, selection */
  --poad-radius: 4px;            /* Corner rounding of controls */
}

/* In dark theme only */
.theme-dark {
  --poad-accent: #3fcf9f;        /* Accent colour: primary button, checked box, selection */
}

/* One area only */
.checkout {
  --poad-radius: 0;              /* Corner rounding of controls */
}
